data.title: Walmart Stock (WMT) Looks Slicker By Helping Customers Save $100 a Year at the Gas Pump
data.description: Shares in retail giant Walmart (WMT) were higher today as it moved to try and help its customers survive soaring gas prices by saving up to $100 a year at the pump. The company revealed that it was adding CITGO sites to its existing Walmart+ gas saving benefit expanding from 13,000 to more than 17,000 participating stations across the U.S. The Walmart share price is down 1.4% in the year-to-date partly as a result of wavering consumer confidence.
data.author: David Craik

data.title: ServiceNow Stock Is Surging Today, Is the Stock Still a Buy? Needham Weighs In
data.description:
AI stocks are down, which therefore means software stocks are up. That scenario appears to be playing out again in Monday's trading following calls from AI leaders to slow down the development of AI.

Against this backdrop, ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) shares, which often seem to move in the opposite direction of AI stalwarts, are up by 8%.

The company has also received a positive assessment from Needham analyst Mike Cikos, who ranks among the top 4% of analysts tracked by TipRanks. Cikos believes investors are becoming more receptive to software stocks as they reassess the importance of established enterprise platforms, the difficulty of displacing leading vendors and the way businesses are making technology purchasing decisions.

After speaking with the company, Cikos came away more positive on its strategy and product roadmap, particularly its opportunity in AI governance. As businesses deploy more AI agents, controlling those systems, monitoring their activity and managing the associated security risks are becoming major challenges. Cikos believes ServiceNow is well placed to address them because of its long-standing role in managing enterprise workflows and IT infrastructure.

One area attracting particular attention is the company's AI Control Tower, which Cikos expects to see sustained adoption as customers look for ways to manage the full lifecycle of AI agents and assess whether their AI investments are delivering meaningful returns.

The 5-star analyst also sees Action Fabric as an important part of ServiceNow's AI strategy. The recent Salesforce-Anthropic Claudeforce initiative highlights a broader change in how enterprises may interact with software, with AI assistants potentially becoming an alternative way to access corporate data and applications. Cikos believes this does not necessarily undermine established software providers. ServiceNow still controls important workflows, data and business processes, while Moveworks remains his "preferred front door" for end users because of its integration with the platform.

More broadly, Cikos sees the rise of AI agents as potentially reinforcing the importance of established enterprise software. Although users might interact with applications through AI rather than traditional interfaces, the underlying data, permissions and workflows still need to sit somewhere. That leaves ServiceNow with an important role in managing those processes as businesses adopt more AI.

Cikos also points to recent customer renewals as another positive signal. ServiceNow's U.S. federal government customers renewed contracts earlier than expected, contributing around 100 basis points to Q2 subscription revenue outperformance. Management said those decisions were not related to pricing changes or new products, which Cikos sees as evidence of underlying customer demand. He believes the renewals also reflect the importance enterprises place on zero-trust security and the potential benefits of ServiceNow's Armis acquisition.

To this end, Cikos rates NOW stock a Buy, while his price target goes from $115 to $155, implying shares will gain 9% over the one-year timeframe. (To watch Cikos' track record, click here)

26 other analysts join Cikos in the bull camp, while 1 Hold and 2 Sells can't detract from a Strong Buy consensus rating. However, the $141.75 average price target suggests the shares are fully valued. (See NOW stock forecast)

data.title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Falls Despite a Quantum Computing Update
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) stock was down 2.96% on Monday, even after the company announced the expansion of an open-source AI project. The chipmaker is expanding its CUDA-Q open-source platform with CUDA-Q Logical, an orchestration layer built to help researchers develop apps for fault-tolerant quantum computers.

According to Nvidia, the new tool lets teams model and manage parts of a quantum system. It also lets them switch between system options to find setups that work well with logical qubits. Nvidia says this could help cut the time needed to build useful quantum-GPU systems.

The need for this work comes from the limits of physical qubits. Fault-tolerant systems use logical qubits to help deal with errors and run larger tasks. Iceberg Quantum used CUDA-Q Logical to model its fault-tolerant design for Diraq's qubits. The work showed that 1,000 logical qubits could be made with 150,000 physical qubits, about 10 times fewer than prior estimates.

Promotion

Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory also used the tool to test qubits, run times and error-correction methods across many system designs. The lab cut its work time from about five months to three weeks. On that same note, Sandia National Laboratories is using CUDA-Q as part of QUOPS, a new open benchmark for tracking the gains made by quantum computing systems. Early tests cover QPUs from Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google, IBM (IBM) and Quantinuum (QNT).

"Quantum computing is maturing into an era of logical qubits," said Timothy Costa, vice president and general manager of quantum at Nvidia. He said CUDA-Q Logical gives teams a way to test full systems across qubit types and designs. Nvidia also pointed to wider use of its quantum tools, such as NVQLink, Nvidia Ising and cuQuantum. CUDA-Q Logical is now open on GitHub, while QUOPS also has a public reference build.

Why Was Nvidia Stock Down Today?

Nvidia stock was down despite its quantum computing update today. That's because there are currently heated arguments about AI advancements. Some AI company CEOs are calling for a slowdown in AI development. On the other hand, some company leaders and government officials want AI development to continue at a brisk pace.

Is Nvidia Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for Nvidia is Strong Buy, based on 30 Buy ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average NVDA stock price target of $324.30, representing a potential 52.72% upside for the shares. (See NVDA Stock Forecast)

data.title: "People Matter More than AI": Microsoft Stock (NASDAQ:MSFT) Gains With New Code of Conduct
data.description:
For a while, tech giant Microsoft (MSFT) looked eager to wedge artificial intelligence (AI) into just about every piece of software it offered, whether it made sense or not. But Microsoft may be pivoting on that idea with a new AI code of conduct, asserting that AI is less important than people. The stance was welcome for investors, and Microsoft stock gained over 2% in Monday afternoon's trading. Microsoft has posted a 3.83% loss in its share price over the past year.

Pulling Back on AI Development

Microsoft's head of AI, Mustafa Suleyman, might well have heard the remarks from CEO Satya Nadella recently. Suleyman toed the line rapidly, declaring that AI must remain under human control. This approach does not come without risks, as slowing development represents the possibility that some capabilities will not be realized at Microsoft. But slowing down also represents the potential for greater public goodwill.

Suleyman noted in an interview with Axios, "I think some people think that it's inevitable that superintelligence is going to exceed human control. But I don't agree with that. I think that would be very, very dangerous, and it means that we're going to have to make decisions about what we're not going to do." Suleyman declared that AI development would be "subordinate to humans," that models would never resist human control, and AI should specifically be designed as a tool.

It turns out that the boot customization option is actually part of a larger set of updates that Microsoft is currently testing. This update set includes things like local search tools, the ability to display badges on your profile—up to five of them—and even some new support for Remote Play. data.title: 'Not That Straightforward Now,' Says Investor About AMD Stock
data.description:
While Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) is hitting the skids today like plenty of its peers, the stock has nevertheless delivered solid returns this year as investors have gained confidence in its position in the AI infrastructure market. The company's latest results reinforced that optimism, with strong growth in data center revenue, improving margins and continued demand for both its server CPUs and AI accelerators.

However, the problem for AMD stock is no longer whether the business is performing well. It is whether the company can continue exceeding the very high expectations already reflected in its share price.

Investor Konstantinos Kosmidis believes the long-term bull case remains intact, but argues that AMD is unlikely to receive another major valuation boost in the near term without a significant upside surprise.

The investor points to a series of events earlier in the year that helped reset expectations around AMD. Strong results from TSMC provided evidence that AI-related chip demand remained robust, while Intel's results suggested that AI inference was creating a larger opportunity for server CPUs than previously expected. Microsoft and Meta then added further support by raising their capital spending plans, reinforcing expectations for continued AI infrastructure investment.

AMD's own first-quarter results provided the clearest confirmation. Data center revenue jumped 57% year-over-year to $5.8 billion, while operating income in the segment rose 72%. Management also forecast second-quarter revenue of around $11.2 billion, ahead of Wall Street expectations. The shares responded by surging almost 19% in the subsequent session.

That reaction, however, meant a substantial amount of good news was already reflected in the stock. The Q2 results were again impressive. Revenue reached a record $11.5 billion, up 50% YoY, while data center revenue more than doubled to $6.7 billion. Gross and operating margins also improved.

Yet the shares failed to enjoy another major rerating because expectations had moved even higher. AMD's forecast for roughly $13 billion of Q3 revenue was above consensus, but investors had already been looking for something more spectacular. The 56% gross margin forecast also suggested limited near-term margin expansion.

With AMD now trading toward the upper end of its recent historical valuation range, the investor believes the stock is fairly valued rather than obviously cheap.

That does not make Konstantinos bearish. AMD's longer-term opportunity remains substantial, with CEO Lisa Su pointing to data center growth of more than 100% in 2027 as the Helios and MI450 platforms ramp. AMD also expects the server CPU market to reach around $220 billion by 2030, while its broader addressable market could reach between $2 trillion and 3 trillion.

For the investor, the key distinction is therefore between a strong business and an attractive entry point. AMD's fundamentals continue to support the bull case, but the stock now needs further evidence of upside to justify another significant rerating.

As such, Konstantinos still sees AMD as a Buy, a rating is a step down from Konstantinos' previous Strong Buy. (To watch Konstantinos' track record, click here)

The analyst consensus, however, still sees the stock as a Strong Buy, a rating based on 29 Buys and 6 Holds. Going by the $645.50 average price target, shares will be changing hands for a 31% premium a year from now. (See AMD stock forecast)

data.title: Why Are AI Infrastructure Stocks Super Micro, CoreWeave, Nebius, and Vertiv Falling Today, Sept. 14?
data.description:
AI infrastructure stocks Super Micro Computer (SMCI), CoreWeave (CRWV), Nebius (NBIS), and Vertiv Holdings (VRT) were down 6.1%, 5.6%, 5.3%, and 7.7%, respectively, at the time of writing on Monday, after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slowdown in the development of AI capabilities, with other major tech CEOs supporting his proposal. Also, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said that his company will not go public in 2026, given growing concerns about AI safety.

Other AI-related stocks were also impacted by the news. Shares of memory companies Micron (MU) and SanDisk (SNDK) fell 5.7% and 5.4%, respectively, while stocks of chip giants Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Nvidia (NVDA), and Intel (INTC) were down 4.6%, 3%, and 4.7%, respectively, at the time of writing.

AI stocks also fell amid broader market pressures as oil prices rose due to persistent tensions in the Middle East and the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5% for the first time since 2023.

Promotion

High conviction CRWV bulls now have this Tradr ETF

Major AI Stocks Hit as CEOs Call for AI Development Slowdown

In an essay on Saturday, Amodei said that AI companies need to slow the pace of innovation for their best models, given safety risks. He also told CBS News that a problem with such a proposal is what would happen if China did not do the same.

Many AI leaders welcomed Amodei's proposal, including OpenAI's Altman, Tesla (TSLA) and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk, and the chair of Google DeepMind (GOOGL).

Furthermore, Amodei proposed a three-step plan to slow the pace of AI development without sacrificing commercial advantage or the U.S.' AI dominance:

  • The first step calls for AI frontier labs to grant third-party evaluators employee-level access to check safety practices and report incidents.
  • The second step encourages leading AI companies within democratic countries to set common safety standards.
  • The third step calls for coordination between democratic and authoritarian governments.

Semiconductor companies such as Nvidia and AMD, neoclouds like Nebius and CoreWeave, and other AI infrastructure providers, including AI server maker Super Micro and power cooling solutions company Vertiv, have been major beneficiaries of AI-driven demand. A potential slowdown in AI development could hurt the businesses of these companies.

Wall Street's Take on SMCI, CRWV, NBIS, and VRT Stocks

According to TipRanks' Stock Comparison Tool, Wall Street has a Strong Buy rating on Vertiv stock and a Moderate Buy rating on CoreWeave and Nebius stocks. Analysts are cautious on Super Micro stock amid concerns about margins, execution risks, and intense competition.

data.title: Dow Jones: DJIA Dips on AI Development Warnings as Rate Hike Odds Advance
data.description:

In an X post, Altman cautioned that humanity "could lose control of the future to AI" without proper safeguards. Furthermore, he said a concentration of AI under one person or company could lead to an "extremely dystopian" outcome.

Meanwhile, Amodei warned in a 3,800-word essay that developing AI irresponsibly could cause economic disruption and more cybersecurity attacks. "We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models," he wrote.

President Trump downplayed the concerns of the two leaders, arguing that the only guardrails necessary are a "STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!" data.title: "Dario Is Right," Tesla Stock (NASDAQ:TSLA) Slips as Elon Musk Joins Concerns About AI
data.description:
Given that electric vehicle giant Tesla (TSLA) makes its own artificial intelligence (AI), which is known as Grok, the idea that Tesla's CEO, Elon Musk, would express concern about AI development seems like it might be counter-productive. But that happened recently, as Musk joined a growing chorus of concern about AI and where it is going. The news rankled shareholders slightly, and Tesla shares dipped fractionally in Monday afternoon's trading. Tesla stock has seen a 10.88% loss in its share price over the past year.

"Dario is Right"

Musk took to X, formerly Twitter, to repost a tweet that Anthropic's CEO, Dario Amodei, posted. The tweet connected to a larger essay, which called for a "slowdown of AI development," as noted by a report from Barron's. The AI development slowdown would be used to help pare back some of the risks connected with AI, ranging from economic calamity, bioterrorism operations, and even cyberattacks like the recent Hugging Face hack.

Musk's own comment in response was simple: "Dario is right." This is a strange development, as a lot of Tesla's operations these days depend on AI and AI development. Everything from Grok to the Cybercabs is dependent on a kind of AI development, and for Musk to even indirectly encourage slowdown leaves his company open to disaster.

"Don't Trust Tesla Summon"

Meanwhile, AI-related quotes hit Tesla from another direction, as drivers were encouraged to not trust Tesla Summon. A Tesla driver recently used the feature, which allows the Tesla to drive itself to your current location from a parking lot. But when his Tesla scraped another vehicle while using it, the driver, who a Motor1 report called "Mr. Wang," revealed the damage. The Tesla scraped a substantial gouge in itself, and also damaged an SUV parked next to it.

data.title: Wall Street's Biggest Bear Just Hiked Their S&P 500 Price Target
data.description:
Bank of America (BAC) analyst Savita Subramanian hiked her 2026 year-end S&P 500 (SPX) price target to 7,400 from 7,100 on Monday. The target implies downside of 2.6% from current levels and is still the lowest among all Wall Street analysts. In addition, Subramanian issued a 12-month SPX target of 7,800.

Subramanian highlighted several risks, including persistent inflation, higher interest rates, and weak seasonality. September is historically the weakest month of the year with an average loss of 0.6%, according to Carson Group.

BofA Warns of Pullback Risk, Slower Earnings Growth in 2027

Furthermore, Subramanian said that stocks are "overdue for a pullback." She pointed out that the S&P 500 has seen just one 5% pullback this year, compared with a historical average of about three per year. On average, the index faces a 10% or greater correction every year, although the last occurrence of this scenario was in spring 2025.
